findings.reason: the author must either cite what holds the services' memory or narrow the bound, or the node spends its hours on a target its own evidence says §61 cannot reach.
findings.text: §72's Why attributes the fleet job's memory pressure to a census of reckon MCP servers (94 servers, 24.8 GB, 10.5 GB under workers), but its deliverable bounds the station, the admit service, the watch producers and a coordinator's server each at under 1 GiB; the cited census does not account for the services' own resident memory. §71 already removes the 10.5 GB the workers' servers hold, and the companion plan's own evidence (the-monitor-reads-each-fact-once §62) says the 1.6 GB ledger decode explained by §61 is one spike, not the 3 GB the station holds after its first tick nor the 0.1–0.3 GB it adds per tick, so the ≤1 GiB station target has no route stated in this plan

findings.reason: the declared wait is the dispatcher's ordering gate, so a bound resting on §62's findings would be built before the section that produces them.
findings.text: the section-dependencies declaration gives §72 the single upstream `the-monitor-reads-each-fact-once#s61`, but the plan that records the station's retained memory is that plan's §62 ("A census names what holds the station's memory"), which §72 neither declares nor cites while it depends on that census's findings to set its bound

findings.reason: a control the node cannot produce leaves §72 unclosable, and the author would replace it with a shorter or attribute-based arm.
findings.text: §72's negative control is "the same readings at the base revision exceed 3 GiB for the admit service", a second two-hour live measurement at a revision that cannot be run once the head has landed and that, at base, is OOM-killed every 4 to 10 minutes (per the companion plan's evidence), so the control is both unobtainable and unable to produce two hours of readings

findings.reason: the record is the one piece of evidence that distinguishes a shared directory from a run-owned path, and unmeasured it can be skipped while the node still closes.
findings.text: §69's Deliverable opens with a clause that the node "first records, from the admission verdicts of §9's window, every crew-home path whose claim held a request and whether a live run owned it", but the Done when tests only the four admission behaviours and never reads that record, and §9's census (§9, plan.html:96) reports only the number of passes holding a request with no claim root

findings.reason: the extension is an instrument with no consumer.
findings.text: §70's Done when adds a third deliverable beyond its two behavioural clauses: §9's census script "extended to attribute each implement run's completion-to-promotion time to its stages", recorded "as the baseline §67 measures against", but §67's Done when (plan.html:342) measures no stage attribution at all — it reports mean working workers, median completion-to-promotion, shared-root holds and identity count — and §70 names no path for the attribution record

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the cross-plan wait `the-monitor-reads-each-fact-once#s61` resolves to that plan's "The lane rate read decodes only its window", and "§9's census script" resolves to the counting script §9 declares under `scripts/` beside its record.
rubric_items.done_when: two findings — §72's negative control requires a two-hour live base-revision measurement that cannot be produced after the head lands, and §69's recording clause has no measure.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every record the changed units name sits on a repository path (`docs/evidence/fragments/work-flows-to-the-lane/s69.html` to `s73.html`, and `docs/evidence/archive/work-flows-to-the-lane-landed.html` for §67).
rubric_items.naming: pass — the changed units introduce no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag into a symbol, file or comment; the `s69`–`s73` fragment names are artifact paths, not source names.
rubric_items.reasoning: two findings — §72 states the MCP-server census as the cause of a bound it places on the services' own memory, and §70 asserts a consumer for the attribution that §67 does not measure.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §70 carries a third deliverable, an extension of §9's census to attribute completion-to-promotion stages, whose stated consumer §67 measures none of it.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §72 declares its only upstream as `the-monitor-reads-each-fact-once#s61`, while the evidence for the station's retained memory sits in that plan's §62, which §72 does not name.
